screens.title: How far one card moves it
screens.prose: Three cards, none shown, fair value 21. The first card turns and shows $c$. The new fair value is $c + 2 \times \dfrac{364 - c}{51}$.
screens.question: Write the change in fair value, new minus 21, in terms of $c$.

explain.text: Over 51 the change is $(51c + 728 - 2c - 1071)/51 = 49(c - 7)/51$. A king gives $49 \times 6/51 = 5.76$, as you found. Each card moves the fair value a little less than its distance from 7.

screens.title: The update rule
screens.prose: You added the cards shown to the unseen cards at the remaining mean. With $k$ of $n$ cards shown, totalling $S$, from a deck of $N$ cards totalling $T$: $$F = S + (n - k)\,\frac{T - S}{N - k}.$$ When $k = n$, $F = S$.
screens.question: Three cards; the first shows an ace. What is the fair value? Give four decimal places.

byKey.seven: You kept the unseen mean at 7. With the ace gone it is 363/51.

explain.text: $F = 1 + 2 \times 363/51 = 15.2353$. An ace leaving raises the remaining mean to 7.12. A low card shown pushes the unseen cards up a little.

widget.solution:
from fractions import Fraction


def card_sum_fair(revealed, n_cards, deck_total=364, deck_size=52):
    """Exact fair value of the sum of n_cards dealt
    without replacement, given the revealed values."""
    k = len(revealed)
    shown = sum(revealed)
    if k == n_cards:
        return Fraction(shown)
    left = Fraction(deck_total - shown, deck_size - k)
    return shown + (n_cards - k) * left


def quote_after_reveals(revealed, n_cards, half_width):
    """(bid, ask) around the fair value before any
    reveal and after each card in revealed."""
    out = []
    for k in range(len(revealed) + 1):
        f = card_sum_fair(revealed[:k], n_cards)
        out.append((f - half_width, f + half_width))
    return out
